wheel.lug_torque: 98 lb-ft (133 N·m), per the 2016 owner's handbook

max_tire.note: LandRoverWorld owners run 265/50R20 with no rubbing; it's also the largest size that fits the spare well inflated. 285/50R20 rubs slightly at full lock and the spare must be deflated to fit. On 18-inch wheels, 265/65R18 doesn't rub at standard height and 285/60R18 brings only mild liner rub at full compression or lock.

One owner ran 275/65R18 and moved to 265/70R18 with lift rods and strut spacers; he reports the 275s sit very close to the upper control arms, and that 12.5-inch-wide 33s are unlikely to fit without rubbing the arms or popping the arch trims.

items.title: Fuel pump outlet flange may crack and leak
items.summary: Covers 3.0 V6 and 5.0 V8 LR4s (and 2010–13 Range Rover Sports): the fuel outlet flange on the tank can crack and leak fuel.

items.title: Panoramic roof adhesive may not hold
items.summary: Trucks built 15 August–18 September 2012 used the wrong primer, so the panoramic roof may not be adequately bonded.

items.title: ABS software can disable stability and descent control
items.summary: An ABS software error on trucks built 19 August 2014–9 February 2015 can disable DSC, Roll Stability Control, traction control and Hill Descent Control.

items.title: Wheel lug nuts may crack
items.summary: Lug nuts on trucks built 6–23 January 2015 may crack and detach from the hub studs.

items.title: TPMS may not learn sensor positions
items.summary: On trucks built 16 September 2013–30 June 2014, the tire-pressure system may not learn sensor locations, so the low-pressure warning may not work properly.

items.title: Driver frontal airbag may not inflate properly
items.summary: A small batch of trucks built 3–10 May 2016.

tsbs.title: 5.0 V8 rattle/click from front of engine: timing chain tensioners and levers
tsbs.summary: 2010–2012 MY LR4, VIN AA513326–CA652214: replace both tensioners (LR051008) and tensioner levers (LR051013); 8.1 h labour allowed.

tsbs.title: AJ133 chain tensioner repeat noise: fit complete revised sets
tsbs.summary: Repeat noise came from partial repairs. Fit both pairs of revised tensioners and steel-insert blades, and never mix old and new parts.

tsbs.title: 2014 MY engine oil cross-contamination (pre-sale update)
tsbs.summary: Some 2014 LR4s (VIN EA705047–EA705560) had 5W-20 mixed with 0W-30 at the factory; the fix was an oil and filter change (LR011279).

tsbs.title: Rear brake squeal when reversing
tsbs.summary: Owners report a warranty TSB with revised rear pads and clips on early trucks; replace the rotors too if they're lipped.

identify.intro: US LR4s are all petrol, but drivetrain content varies a lot by year and option, and the expensive engine fixes are VIN-specific. Know exactly what you're looking at.

items.head: Model year from the VIN
items.body: Land Rover quotes VIN ranges by their last eight characters, which begin with the model-year letter: A = 2010, B = 2011, C = 2012, D = 2013, E = 2014, F = 2015, G = 2016. That's the 10th VIN character under US federal rules. Use it to check a 5.0 V8 against bulletin LTB00474's range AA513326–CA652214.

items.head: Engine
items.body: 2010–2013 US trucks have the 5.0 V8; 2014–2016 have the 3.0 supercharged V6. A diesel Discovery 4 in the US is not a factory US vehicle.

items.head: Low range and rear locker
items.body: All 2010–2013 US trucks have the two-speed transfer box. On 2014–16 trucks, low range and the active rear locker came only with the Heavy Duty package. Owners check the 4x4 information screen (a single centre-lock icon means no HD package), the spare (HD added a full-size one) and the rear diff for the locker's actuator motor. Owners don't agree on whether every 2010–2013 truck has the rear locker, so check physically or with a VIN decode.

items.head: Late trims
items.body: For 2016.5, owners report that the HSE Silver and HSE Landmark replaced the HSE and HSE Lux; Landmark trucks have Landmark badging, bright silver roof rails and 20-inch split-spoke wheels.

items.head: Armoured Sentinel
items.body: Land Rover's factory-armoured Discovery 4 Sentinel (B6 protection) is described as almost indistinguishable from a standard truck, so a heavy, oddly specified D4 deserves a closer look.

values.intro: Cheap for what they are, because buyers price in cooling and chain work. Low-mileage 2015–16 trucks and Landmark editions bring the strongest money.
values.note: Based on 139 Bring a Trailer LR4 sales from January 2025 to October 2026: $4,000–69,000, median about $14,750, middle half $11,250–23,750. The top result was a 1,600-mile 2016 Landmark Edition at $69,000; 16 Landmarks had a median of about $20,000.

paragraphs: Land Rover sold only petrol LR4s in the US, so the TDV6 and SDV6 Discovery 4 diesels are gray-market. NHTSA's 25-year exemption is counted from the date of manufacture, and the first Discovery 4s were built in 2009, so the earliest diesels won't become eligible until 2034. Until then, a US-registered diesel D4 should be treated with suspicion.
